title: ICJ advisory opinion on climate obligations
article: Obligations of States in respect of climate change

definition.text: A 2025 advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice on what international law requires states to do to protect the climate, requested by the UN General Assembly in 2023.

facts.text: The request, led by Vanuatu and driven by Pacific island students, was adopted by the General Assembly by consensus on 29 March 2023.
The Court unanimously held that the UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement create binding obligations, including submitting NDCs and acting on common but differentiated responsibilities.
Failing to meet these obligations is an internationally wrongful act that can require cessation, guarantees of non-repetition and full reparation, given a clear causal link.
Because the climate is a global common good, any state may invoke another's responsibility for breaches; the opinion is not binding but is expected to be used in courts.

prerequisites: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

title: Pledge and review

definition.text: A way of organising international climate action in which each country makes its own pledge, others review its progress, and stronger pledges follow.

facts.text: It is a 'bottom-up' approach, unlike legally binding targets imposed 'top-down' by a central body.
Japan first proposed it in 1991; it was rejected at the first COP in 1995 in favour of binding targets, which led to the Kyoto Protocol.
Revived at Copenhagen in 2009, it drew pledges from countries producing about 80% of global emissions, versus 25% covered by Kyoto's first targets.
By 2015 it was the central approach, though at Paris the pledges were renamed Nationally Determined Contributions.
It became dominant because binding greenhouse-gas targets proved hard to agree and impossible to enforce on powerful nations.
Critics called it 'hedge and retreat' or 'second best', while others called it an essential pillar of mitigation.

prerequisites: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
contested_note: Environmental groups and some academics have called pledge-and-review inadequate, while other academics see it as essential.

definition.text: A loan with an interest rate below the market rate.

facts.text: It may also offer other concessions, such as long repayment periods or interest holidays.
Governments usually give soft loans to projects they consider worthwhile, and the World Bank and other development institutions give them to developing countries.
Some official development assistance is counted as the concessional value of soft loans.
